name: ViT deepfake-vs-real face classifier (dima806)
reason: Measured locally and rejected for manipulation detection: on face-focused SBI pairs the member scored at chance (AUROC ~0.51 over 45 samples) while real aged portraits hit 99-100 fake (FPR@50 ~0.47). See experiments/FACESWAP_EVALUATION.md and experiments/eval_face_manipulation.py. The model's trained task — fully AI-generated faces vs real photos — is a different problem than faceswap.
limitations: Weights are not committed; transformers downloads the ~330 MB ViT snapshot from the hub_model id on first use (or set hub_model to a local snapshot directory for offline runs).
DISABLED: measured at chance on face-focused SBI manipulation pairs (AUROC ~0.51) with ~47% FPR driven by aged portraits scoring 99-100 fake — kept as a documented candidate, not an active member.
Trained on real-vs-synthetic face imagery — its actual domain is fully generated faces; pixel-level self-blend manipulations on real photos are out-of-scope and measured accordingly.
Scores are a prioritization signal, not a truth label; absence of a detected face makes this member inapplicable rather than a 'real' verdict — and a detector miss silently reduces coverage.
notes: Runtime 'hf-image-classifier' uses AutoImageProcessor + AutoModelForImageClassification; 'score_label' resolves the softmax index from the model's id2label so label order cannot silently flip the score.
Local check (2026-09): lenna-face.png -> Real 0.992, lenna-face-sbi.png -> Fake 0.783 — a 3-image smoke test that did NOT survive a labeled eval set (5 portraits x SBI x 3 variants -> AUROC ~0.51).

Both community face checkpoints tried so far failed local measurement (this one and the rejected efficientnet-b0-ffpp-c23); faceswap coverage remains an open gap — see FACESWAP_EVALUATION.md for candidate directions.
